item.title: Mini crackme: bswap + xor
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Windows x64 calling convention. `check(unsigned x)` receives `x` in ECX and returns 1 in AL if accepted.
``` check: bswap ecx xor ecx, 0x3C3C3C3C cmp ecx, 0x446A082E sete al ret ```
What value of `x` makes `check` return 1?
---
**Answer: x = 0x12345678 (305419896)**
1. `bswap` reverses the four bytes of ECX (little-endian <-> big-endian swap), so the check is bswap(x) ^ 0x3C3C3C3C == 0x446A082E. 2. Undo in reverse order: 0x446A082E ^ 0x3C3C3C3C = 0x78563412 (XOR is self-inverse). 3. `bswap` is also its own inverse, so swapping 0x78563412 gives x = 0x12345678.
